title: My Grace Is Sufficient: The Three Words That Carry You When Everything Else Falls Apart
paragraphs:
My Grace Is Sufficient: The Three Words That Carry You When Everything Else Falls Apart
When God Doesn't Remove the Thorn, He Reveals Something Better Than Relief
There are moments in life when we do not need another sermon, another motivational quote, or another promise that everything will work out.
We need an answer.
A real answer.

The kind that comes in the middle of sleepless nights, unanswered prayers, broken relationships, financial pressure, hidden struggles, chronic pain, overwhelming anxiety, grief that refuses to leave, and battles that seem to follow us year after year.
Many believers know what it feels like to ask God the same question repeatedly:
"Lord, why won't You take this away?"
The Apostle Paul knew that feeling.
And what God told him has become one of the most quoted promises in all of Scripture.
Yet it is also one of the most misunderstood.
The words are found in 2 Corinthians 12:9:
"And He said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness."
Behind our English translations stands the original Greek text:
"Καὶ εἴρηκέν μοι· Ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου, ἡ γὰρ δύναμίς μου ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ τελεῖται."
Transliterated:
"Arkei soi hē charis mou, hē gar dynamis mou en astheneia teleitai."
Literally:
"Sufficient for you is My grace, for My power is brought to completion in weakness."
Notice what God did not say.
He did not say:
"My solution is sufficient."
"My miracle is sufficient."
"My healing is sufficient."
"My deliverance is sufficient."
He said:
"My grace."
The Greek word χάρις (charis) means favor, kindness, divine empowerment, unearned blessing, and God's active presence working in the life of someone who could never deserve it.
Grace is not merely God's forgiveness.
Grace is God's sustaining power.
Grace is not only what saves you.
Grace is what carries you when you feel like you cannot take another step.
Paul had pleaded with God three times to remove what he called a "thorn in the flesh."
Scholars have debated its exact nature for centuries. Some believe it was physical suffering. Others suggest persecution, weakness, or an ongoing affliction.
Scripture never specifically identifies it.
Perhaps that is intentional.
Because if God had named it, only some people would relate.
By leaving it unnamed, every hurting person sees themselves in Paul's story.
Your thorn may be depression.
It may be betrayal.
It may be regret.
It may be addiction.
It may be loneliness.
It may be a prodigal child.
It may be a marriage hanging by a thread.
It may be a secret battle no one knows exists.
Whatever it is, Paul's cry becomes our cry.
And God's answer becomes our answer.
"My grace is sufficient."
The Greek word translated "sufficient" is ἀρκεῖ (arkei).
It means enough.
Adequate.
Completely sufficient.
Lacking nothing.
God was saying:
"Paul, what I am giving you is enough for what you are facing."
Not because the suffering was small.
But because God's grace was greater.
This truth echoes throughout Scripture.
When Moses felt inadequate, God was enough.
When David faced Goliath, God was enough.
When Daniel entered the lions' den, God was enough.
When Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego entered the fire, God was enough.
When Peter sank beneath the waves, God was enough.
When Paul sat in prison, God was enough.
And when Jesus hung upon the cross carrying the sins of the world, the grace of God was still unfolding a redemption story greater than anyone could imagine.
The Hebrew concept behind grace is often connected to the word חֵן (chen), meaning favor, acceptance, and kindness bestowed by God.
But biblical grace is never passive.
Grace moves.
Grace pursues.
Grace rescues.
Grace transforms.
Grace rewrites.
That is why the Gospel itself is the greatest scandal-to-grace story ever told.
Humanity rebelled.
Humanity fell.
Humanity sinned.
Yet God did not abandon His creation.
John 1:14 says:
"And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us."
The Greek reads:
"Καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο."
"Kai ho Logos sarx egeneto."
The eternal Word became flesh.
Jesus stepped into our scandal.
He entered our brokenness.
He walked among sinners.
Touched lepers.
Welcomed outcasts.
Forgave adulterers.
Restored failures.
Loved enemies.
Carried our sins.
And died the death we deserved.
Then He rose again.
The Gospel is not the story of good people becoming better.
It is the story of dead people being made alive.
The story of grace reaching where religion cannot.
The story of mercy triumphing over judgment.
The story of God rewriting everything.
That is why Paul's weakness became a platform for God's glory.
Because weakness reveals dependence.
Dependence reveals faith.
Faith reveals God's power.
The world tells us to hide our weakness.
God tells us to bring it to Him.
The world celebrates self-sufficiency.
The Kingdom celebrates Christ-sufficiency.
The world says, "You are enough."
Jesus says, "Apart from Me you can do nothing" (John 15:5).
And strangely, that truth is not crushing.
It is freeing.
Because if everything depends on us, we will eventually break.
But if everything depends on Christ, there is hope even in our lowest moments.
Perhaps that is why some of the people most powerfully used by God are those who have been shattered by life.
Because brokenness often becomes the doorway through which grace enters most deeply.
Maybe you clicked on this article because you are exhausted.
Maybe you have prayed and prayed and prayed.
Maybe you are wondering if God sees you.
Maybe you are questioning whether He still has a purpose for your life.
Hear His words again:
"My grace is sufficient for you."
Not will be.
Is.
Present tense.
Right now.
Today.
In this moment.
For this struggle.
For this battle.
For this burden.
For this season.
His grace is enough.
Not because your problem is small.
But because your Savior is great.
And that changes everything.
If this message spoke directly to your heart, don't keep it to yourself.
Someone in your family may need this reminder tonight.
Someone may be waiting for a word from God and not even realize it.
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs.
Because every share spreads the Gospel.
Every comment encourages a soul.
Every tag reaches someone searching for hope.
And every act of faith becomes another reminder that God's grace is still changing lives.
One day you will discover that the thorn you begged God to remove became the very place where you learned His grace was enough.
And that grace will tell a better story than comfort ever could.
The scars you wanted erased may become the testimony that leads someone else to Jesus.
